items.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024
items.q: Emile Charlap was a New York contractor. He used to copy all my music for me, and he would show me what I did wrong and what I did right.

ctx.x: These were guys in the band?

No, they was New York — Emile Charlap was a New York contractor. He used to copy all my music for me, and he would show me what I did wrong and what I did right. You know I used to write all the parts out and I saw Dave Matthews, he was a fine arranger you know. And I would write things over and over again and he would draw lines, you know, from one part to another. You know and I said, “Can you do that?” And he said, “Yeah, you can do that.” And Emile would write it, he would transpose it for them you know, and…
I can picture that because I was listening to “Pass the Peas” you know, and you’ve got that line [scats]. You could just write it once and put 8 times.
